title: KYE Protocol Trademarks Registry
description: Machine-readable registry of KYE Protocol™ protected marks. Consumed by scripts/audit-trademarks.mjs to enforce first-prominent-use ™ on every public surface, and by downstream tooling (license generators, conformance attestation forms) that need to programmatically reference the marks. 2026-05-28: KYE Counterparty Governance Rail™ and KYE Runtime Console™ marks added to the public registries (additive entries only — this schema unchanged at the structural level; the description field bump is the lockstep marker for the §53 §3.3 schema-existence triplet). 2026-05-30 (Wave-AgenticGovernanceMarks): the 4 positioning marks Agentic Governance™, Agent Governance™, Agentic Era™, Agentic Governance Protocol™ added to both registries; structurally additive only; lockstep marker bumped. 2026-06-20 (KYE Academy authority tracks): the capstone certification mark KYE Certified Agentic Governance Practitioner™ added to both registries; structurally additive only; lockstep marker bumped. 2026-06-24 (Governed Organization marks): KYE Governed Organization™ + KYE Certified Governed Organization™ (the §66 entity-level certificate family, kind=organization) added to both registries; structurally additive only; lockstep marker bumped.

enforcement_mode.description: Structured, machine-readable form of policy.rule. The trademark audit MUST derive its enforcement behaviour from this field rather than hand-coding a rule beside the prose (no-hand-rolling; machine-readable-by-default). 'first-prominent-use' = only the first prose occurrence of a mark per page must carry the symbol; 'every-occurrence' = every prose occurrence must.

compound_exception.description: When a registered mark appears as a substring of a longer compound name that itself carries the symbol, the substring does not need its own. Present in the instance since adoption; added to the schema 2026-08-17 to close a schema/instance drift that additionalProperties:false would otherwise reject.

classes.description: Reading order, label and description per mark class — the ONE declaration the public renderer iterates (§0.55 sets resolve, they are never enumerated). It replaced a CAT_ORDER/CAT_LABEL/CAT_DESC literal in public/site/assets/inline/b-6dc29c920eba.js that named 11 of the 21 classes marks[] actually uses and silently skipped the rest, so 32 of 363 marks — every rule-pack mark among them — never rendered on the page whose purpose is listing them.

class.description: A value appearing in marks[].class. audit-trademarks resolves that set and refuses a mark whose class no row here declares.

label.description: Section heading on the public page.

classes_note.description: Why classes[] exists, kept beside it so the reason travels with the data.

sku_id.description: The §26 SKU identifier this mark is attached to. Constrained so a mark cannot claim a SKU from outside the KYE catalogue namespace.

enforcement.description: Names the gate that enforces this contract so contract and enforcer are discoverable from each other. Shape mirrors the pre-existing enforcement{} block in the deploy-toolchain registry rather than introducing a new pattern.

derives_from.description: Contract fields the enforcer MUST read rather than re-implement. A field listed here that the enforcer never references is a contract/enforcer split.
